paper_metadata.title: Mechanical property and strengthening mechanism of ZrC nanoparticle dispersion-strengthened Mo containing FeCrAl alloys

evidence.quote: Fe-13Cr-5Al (wt %) alloys were strengthened by adding solid solution element Mo and nanosized ZrC particles, and the strengthening mechanism was assessed by microstructure characterizations including TEM and EBSD.

evidence.quote: signals from Zr, C, Al and O are detected in the bright nanoparticles (see right and bottom picture in Fig. 6), suggesting that the nanoparticles dispersed either inside the grains or at grain boundaries in FeCrAlMo-ZrC alloy are ZrC particles and alumina particles.

attributes.morphology: inhomogeneous, coarse and fine equiaxed grains

evidence.quote: FeCrAl samples without Mo and ZrC nanoparticles additions show an inhomogeneous grain structure which is composed of some several coarse equiaxed grains and a large number of fine equiaxed grains... The average grain size of FeCrAl is about 2.53 μm.

attributes.morphology: inhomogeneous, similar to FeCrAl but refined

evidence.quote: FeCrAlMo-ZrC samples exhibit the similar structure, as shown in Fig. 4 (b), however the average grain size of FeCrAlMo-ZrC refined significantly to 0.49 μm
there are high-density dislocation tangles in some grains marked by red dotted box as shown in Fig. 5 (b).
all the samples exhibit a ductile dimple fracture mode during tensile testing. The dimples in FeCrAl alloy are larger and deeper, implying a good ductility.
in FeCrAlMo-ZrC sample, there are some cleavages observed in the fracture surfaces, implying a lower ductility

The excellent mechanical properties and superior thermal stabilities of Fe-13Cr-5Al-2Mo-1ZrC alloy were not only attributed to the dispersion strengthen by nanosized ZrC particles, the solid solution strengthening by Mo elements, but also the grain refinement structure promoted by the synergistic effects of Mo and ZrC additions.

Fine grain strengthening is due to synergistic effects of MO and ZrC additions.
the superior thermal stability of FeCrAl based alloys is originated from the Zener pinning mechanism of the nanoparticles on the grain boundaries

Solid solution strengthening by Mo elements, precipitation strengthening by ZrC nano-sized particles and fine grain strengthening by the synergistic effects of Mo and ZrC additions are the strengthening mechanisms for the FeCrAl based alloy especially at high temperature.
